The table summarizes the UV index value recorded by a research assistant at noon each day for 49 days.
UV indexNumber of days
19

413
According to the table, a UV index value of 1 was recorded on how many days?
whyCorrect: Read the row whose UV index is 1 and take the value in the second column. That column counts days, so 9 days had a UV index of 1. No arithmetic is needed; the trap is reading the wrong column or adding rows together.

whyWrong.A: 4 is the largest UV index in the first column, not a count of days.
whyWrong.C: 40 is the total number of days for indexes 2, 3 and 4 combined — the days that were not index 1.
whyWrong.D: 49 is the total number of days observed, the sum of the whole second column.

whyCorrect: "Maximum" means the largest single value in the data, not the largest possible reading on the scale and not an average. Compare the four counts and take the biggest: 100, at Plot 3.

whyWrong.D: 78 is Plot 4, the minimum rather than the maximum.

stem: The dot plot shown gives the distribution of values in a data set. What is the minimum value in the data set?
whyCorrect: The minimum is the smallest value that actually occurs, so read the position of the leftmost column of dots on the number line, not how many dots are stacked there. The leftmost stack sits at 11, so the minimum value is 11.

whyWrong.A: 1 is not a value on the number line at all; it looks like the count of the shortest stack.
whyWrong.B: 2 is the height of the leftmost stack — how many times 11 occurs, not the value itself.
whyWrong.C: 9 is a tick on the axis with no dots above it, so no data point takes that value.

note: Dot plot on a number line labelled 10-17. Dot counts: 11 -> 2, 12 -> 3, 13 -> 5, 14 -> 5, 15 -> 4, 16 -> 1 (no dots at 10 or 17), 20 values in total. Not converted to a table because questions 13 and 15 in the same section are the same question presented as a frequency table.

whyCorrect: The data set is the values in the left column, each repeated as many times as the right column says. The frequency column never contributes a data value, so the minimum is the smallest entry in the Value column: 11.

whyWrong.A: 1 is the smallest number in the Frequency column — it is how often 18 occurs, not a value in the data set.
whyWrong.B: 9 is a frequency, not a value.
whyWrong.D: 18 is a value in the data set but not the smallest one; 11 is smaller.

stem:
1, 4, 7, 10, 33

What is the mean of the data shown?
whyCorrect: Add all five values and divide by 5: 1 + 4 + 7 + 10 + 33 = 55, and 55 ÷ 5 = 11. The single large value, 33, pulls the mean above the middle value, which is why the mean here is not the same as the median.

whyWrong.A: 7 is the median — the middle value once the list is ordered — not the mean.
whyWrong.C: 17 is the mean of just the smallest and largest values, (1 + 33) ÷ 2; it ignores the other three numbers.
whyWrong.D: 33 is the largest value, i.e. the maximum, not an average.

The tables summarize the distributions of scores for team A and team B.
ScoreFrequency, team AFrequency, team B
20 to 25032
25 to 304224
30 to 354811
35 to 404311
40 to 45024
45 to 50032
Which statement best compares the standard deviations of scores for these teams?

choices.label: A
choices.content: The standard deviation of scores for team A is less than the standard deviation of scores for team B.

choices.label: B
choices.content: The standard deviation of scores for team A is greater than the standard deviation of scores for team B.

choices.label: C
choices.content: The standard deviation of scores for team A is equal to the standard deviation of scores for team B.

choices.label: D
choices.content: There is not enough information to compare the standard deviations.

whyCorrect: Standard deviation measures how far the values sit from their own mean, so you compare spread, not centre or total. Team A's scores all fall between 25 and 40 and pile up in the middle of that band, while team B's scores run from 20 to 50 with the biggest groups at the two ends and a dip in the middle. Values clustered near the centre give a small standard deviation; values pushed out to both extremes give a large one, so team A's is the smaller.

whyWrong.B: This reverses the comparison. Team A looks taller only because its scores are packed into fewer intervals, and bar height is frequency, not spread.
whyWrong.C: The two distributions have visibly different shapes — one tightly clustered, one spread to both ends — so their standard deviations cannot be equal.
whyWrong.D: The full distribution of both teams is given, which is everything the standard deviation depends on, so it can be compared.

note: Source prints two histograms (Frequency against Score, 20-50 in width-5 bins). Bar heights read off the graph and are approximate, but the question only compares spread, so the comparison is unaffected.

The table shows the distribution of heights, in centimeters, of 25 objects.
HeightFrequency
0 to 1008
101 to 2006
201 to 3005
301 to 4004
401 to 5002
Which of the following could be the median height of these objects?
whyCorrect: With 25 values the median is the 13th one when they are ordered, since 12 lie below it and 12 above. Add the frequencies from the top until you pass 13: the first interval covers values 1 through 8, and the second covers values 9 through 14. The 13th value therefore lies in the 101 to 200 interval, and 155 is the only choice in that range.

whyWrong.A: 355 sits in 301 to 400, which holds only values 20 through 23 — far past the middle.
whyWrong.B: 255 sits in 201 to 300, which holds values 15 through 19; the 13th value has already been reached before that interval starts.
whyWrong.D: 55 sits in 0 to 100, which holds only the first 8 values, so it stops short of the 13th.

note: Book prints "heights of, centimeters, of 25 objects"; read as "heights, in centimeters, of 25 objects".

Scientists collected acorns that each housed a colony of a particular species and then analyzed each colony's structure. For these colonies, the table summarizes the number of queen ants per colony. For these colonies, what is the median number of queen ants per colony?
whyCorrect: The individuals being ordered are the colonies, not the five rows. Add the second column: 11 + 9 + 7 + 6 + 6 = 39 colonies, so the median is the 20th colony once they are lined up from fewest queens to most. The first 11 colonies have 1 queen and colonies 12 through 20 have 2 queens, so the 20th colony has 2 queen ants.

whyWrong.A: 6 is a frequency from the second column, not a number of queen ants.
whyWrong.B: 4 comes from averaging or from taking the middle of the numbers 1 through 5 without weighting each by how many colonies it represents.
whyWrong.C: 3 is the middle row of the table, but the rows are not equally common — 20 of the 39 colonies have 1 or 2 queens, which drags the median down.
